name: Northwest Couloir

waypoints.name: Cathedral Rock Trailhead (Trail #1345)
waypoints.directions: From I-90 take Exit 80 (Roslyn/Salmon la Sac), follow Bullfrog Road to the roundabout, then SR-903 north through Roslyn and Ronald along Cle Elum Lake to Salmon la Sac. Bear right just before the campground onto gravel Cle Elum Valley Road (FR 4330) and drive about 12 miles to the Cathedral Rock Trailhead (#1345) near Tucquala Meadows, at about 3,350 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park; fill out the free self-issue wilderness permit.

waypoints.name: Nosh Nosh Wahtum (formerly Squaw Lake) — water and campsites
waypoints.directions: Take Trail #1345 west, crossing the Cle Elum River on a footbridge near the start, then climb steadily through forest. Continue straight at the Trail Creek Trail #1332 junction at about 2 miles; the trail reaches Nosh Nosh Wahtum and its campsites along the lake's northeast shore at about 2.5 miles.

waypoints.name: Cathedral Pass / Pacific Crest Trail junction
waypoints.directions: Continue on Trail #1345 past the lake, up through subalpine meadow and then steeper, rockier switchbacks to Cathedral Pass and the Pacific Crest Trail junction at about 5,550 ft, roughly 4 miles from the car.

waypoints.name: Peggy's Pond — standard base camp and water source
waypoints.directions: Join the PCT southbound toward Deep Lake for a few tenths of a mile. At the first switchback where it starts down toward Deep Lake, take the Peggy's Pond trail #1375, a primitive path that traverses beneath Cathedral Rock to the pond. The last stretch is narrow and steep with real drop-offs and loose rock, and holds snow into early summer.

waypoints.name: Cathedral Rock summit
waypoints.directions: Traverse around the pond, then climb heather and small trees onto the northwest flank and loose rubble in the lower corral to the top of the funnel. Follow a dirty ledge rightward to the couloir entrance about 200 ft south of the funnel, stem past the chockstone in the enclosed chimney, then climb the couloir and a sloping slab using a big flake as a handrail. Broken slopes lead to the summit.

itinerary: Best done as an overnight. Day one: hike 4.5 miles to Peggy's Pond (about 2,300 ft of gain) and camp. Day two: climb the northwest couloir in a half day from camp — one recorded party left camp with two hours of light remaining and was on the summit before dusk and back at the pond before dark — then pack up and walk out the same day. It also works as a long single day from the car if you are fit, and pairs naturally with Mount Daniel from the same Peggy's Pond camp.
descent_text: The trip-report party reversed the route, downclimbing the chimney and couloir and then descending via separate open books and scree slopes back to Peggy's Pond, using an existing rappel ring anchor (and finding an old piton with an REI oval) near the top. If you are reversing the couloir, treat the chockstone chimney as the crux of the descent and rappel it rather than fighting it downwards with a pack. The alternative — and the better option if you are heading for the trailhead rather than a camp at the pond — is to descend the ordinary Southwest Face: scramble the ridge crest southwest, make one or two rappels off the rock horn with fixed slings and rings, downclimb the main gully, and walk back to Cathedral Pass. Either way, inspect any fixed anchor you find; the tat and hardware on this peak is old.
